title: HCLTech Hiring Process Experience – AI Engineer Role
author: ARNAV RAJVANSHI
body:
The HCLTech hiring process consisted of two rounds: an AI-based interview conducted through Berribot, followed by a hackathon.

Round 1: AI Interview (Berribot)

The first round was an AI-driven interview designed to assess core IT fundamentals, programming knowledge, and problem-solving abilities. The questions ranged from easy to intermediate difficulty and covered fundamental IT concepts, along with coding questions in Python and SQL. Overall, the round tested both theoretical understanding and practical programming skills.

Round 2: Hackathon

The second round was a hackathon that simulated a corporate product development environment. For the AI Engineer role, the hackathon featured three use cases centered on multi-agent architectures using LangGraph and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines. Participants were required to develop solutions while following a structured software development lifecycle.

The process included three project presentations at different stages of development, during which participants had to explain their approach, demonstrate progress, and justify their implementation and design decisions.

In addition to project development, participants were evaluated on their understanding of the fundamentals of RAG, agentic systems, and AI. This assessment focused on the underlying concepts behind the solutions, including how RAG pipelines work, how AI agents interact and coordinate tasks, and the principles guiding the design of AI-driven systems. Thus, the hackathon assessed both the ability to build functional solutions and the conceptual understanding required to design them effectively.

Overall Experience

The hiring process combined a fundamental technical assessment with practical AI solution development. While the Berribot interview focused on core IT knowledge and programming proficiency, the hackathon evaluated technical implementation, conceptual clarity in AI and agentic architectures, and the ability to follow a structured development lifecycle. Overall, it was a valuable experience that offered insight into how AI-driven products are developed, evaluated, and presented in a professional environment.

title: HCLTech Interview Experience
author: MOHIT RANJAN
body:
My HCLTech selection process was divided into three major stages: the AI Interview on BerryBot, the Hackathon Round, and the HR Round.

1. AI Interview – BerryBot

Before the hackathon, we had an AI-based interview on the BerryBot platform.

The interview was mainly based on my resume, projects, technical skills, and previous experiences. The AI asked questions related to the technologies and projects mentioned in my resume and also asked follow-up questions based on my responses.

So, my suggestion for this round is to prepare your resume properly. You should be able to explain every project, technology, internship, and skill that you have mentioned.

After the BerryBot interview, shortlisted candidates were selected for the next stage, which was the HCLTech Hackathon.

2. HCLTech Hackathon Experience

The hackathon started at around 10:00 AM. At the beginning, we were given a problem statement and approximately one hour for design thinking and solution planning.

During this one hour, our team discussed the complete approach, architecture, workflow, technologies, and models that we planned to use. We prepared a PPT explaining our proposed solution.

The evaluators were continuously interacting with the teams during the hackathon. They would come to our table, check our progress, ask what we were working on, understand our approach, and also ask whether we required any help.

After approximately one hour, we presented our design and PPT to the evaluators. They asked several questions regarding our solution. A major focus was on the technical choices.

For example, they asked questions such as:

- Why are you using this particular technology?

- Why did you select this model?

- Why this model instead of another model?

- What would be the difference if you used another approach?

- Why is your proposed tech stack suitable for this problem?

They sometimes intentionally cross-questioned us to check whether we actually understood the technologies we were proposing or were simply mentioning them.

After our design was approved, we were asked to start implementing the solution.

During the implementation phase, another evaluator came and asked me several Machine Learning and AI fundamentals, including topics such as:

- Bias and Variance

- BM25

- Embeddings

- Chunking

- RAG

- Basic Machine Learning concepts

These questions were also part of the evaluation and marks were given based on our answers.

Later, another evaluator came for a progress review. He asked us to explain:

- What we had implemented

- How the solution was working

- What technologies we had used

- How different components were connected

He also asked me a SQL question during the interaction.

The hackathon continued with multiple reviews like this, where evaluators checked both our technical knowledge and our implementation progress.

At around 4:00 PM, we were called for the final demonstration on the third floor of the library.

During the final presentation, we demonstrated the complete working solution. We showed different test cases, explained the overall workflow, demonstrated the features we had implemented, and answered questions related to our solution.

The evaluators also asked a few questions regarding our code and implementation.

After the final demonstration, they told us that our evaluation was complete and we could leave.

3. HR Round

Approximately one hour after the hackathon, I received a call for the HR Round.

The HR round was comparatively simple and conversational. They asked basic questions such as:

- Tell me about yourself.

- What is your name?

- Where are you from?

- Questions related to my background.

- General HR and personality-related questions.

My suggestion is to prepare at least one good question to ask the HR at the end of the interview. It creates a good impression and shows that you are genuinely interested in the organization and the role.

My Suggestions for Future Candidates

The most important thing during the hackathon and interview is to communicate confidently and clearly.

Even if you do not know everything, do not become silent or nervous. Be open and explain whatever you understand. If you know something, present it properly and confidently.

During a hackathon, technical knowledge is important, but your ability to present your solution, explain your decisions, communicate with evaluators, and handle cross-questions is equally important.

You should be able to market your skills properly. The evaluators can only understand your capabilities if you explain what you have done and why you have done it.

So, during the hackathon:

- Be active and communicate with the evaluators.

- Clearly explain your contribution.

- Know the reason behind every technology and model you use.

- Be prepared for cross-questioning.

- Revise basic ML, AI, SQL, RAG, and project-related concepts.

- Prepare your resume thoroughly for the AI interview.

- Present your final solution with proper test cases.

- Stay confident even if you do not know the answer to every question.

- Prepare one meaningful question for the HR round.

Overall, the HCLTech process was not only about building a solution. They were evaluating our technical fundamentals, problem-solving approach, communication skills, teamwork, implementation ability, and confidence throughout the process.

title: HCLTech AI Engineer Interview Experience & Selection Process
author: AKASH CHOWDHURY
body:
I recently participated in the recruitment drive for the AI Engineer role at HCLTech and am thrilled to share that I was selected! The evaluation process was highly practical, focusing more on hands-on application rather than just theoretical knowledge. Here is a brief breakdown of my experience:

Round 1: Berribot Interview The hiring process began with an automated Berribot interview. This served as the initial screening phase, where a conversational AI bot asked preliminary questions to assess my foundational technical knowledge, problem-solving abilities, and communication skills. It was a unique, fast-paced round that tested my ability to articulate answers clearly to an automated system.

Round 2: Hackathon Round (Case Study) After clearing the initial screening, I advanced to the core technical phase: a single-day Hackathon. We were assigned a complex, real-world AI case study and given one day to develop a working solution. This round was intense and thoroughly tested my ability to rapidly understand a problem statement, clean data, select the right algorithms, and build a viable machine learning pipeline under strict time constraints.

Round 3: Final Solution Demo The final stage was a live presentation of the project I built during the hackathon. I had to give a proper demo of my solution to the technical panel. The interviewers evaluated not just whether the code worked, but how I approached the problem. We had a detailed discussion about my technical choices, model architecture, edge cases, and potential optimizations.

Final Tips for Aspirants If you are preparing for this role, focus heavily on your practical coding skills and building end-to-end projects. The panel cares deeply about your ability to deliver a working solution and confidently explain the "why" behind your technical decisions during the final demo. Best of luck!

author: ISHIKA GAMBHIR
body:
HCLTech Placement Experience

I recently got placed at HCLTech, and I wanted to share my overall interview experience to help others preparing for the recruitment process.

The selection process consisted of three rounds.

Round 1: AI Bot Interview (Technical + Communication)

The first round was an AI-based interview conducted by a bot.

It started with a basic self-introduction, followed by questions about my projects, including the technologies I used and my contributions.

I was also asked to solve:

1 DSA coding question
1 SQL query

Overall, this round mainly evaluated our communication skills, coding knowledge, and ability to explain our projects clearly.

Round 2: Hackathon + Technical Interview

The second round was a hackathon where we were given two case studies, and each team had to select one.

Our team chose RetailPulse AI.

Throughout the hackathon, mentors and evaluators visited our team at regular intervals, almost every hour, to monitor our progress.

They asked questions such as:

How did you approach the problem?
How did you implement this functionality?
Can you explain your code?
Why did you choose this particular approach?

Even though we were allowed to use AI tools for development, we were expected to understand the code, explain the implementation, and justify our technical decisions.

After the development phase, we had a group evaluation, where our project was tested for its functionality and overall implementation. We were also given two additional use cases to evaluate how well our solution could handle new requirements.

Following this, we had an individual technical interview.

In my interview, I was mainly asked questions from:

SQL
Object-Oriented Programming (OOPs)
Operating Systems (OS)

The questions focused on fundamental concepts and understanding rather than just memorized definitions.

Round 3: HR Interview

The final round was an HR interview, which was a non-elimination round.

It was mainly a general interaction to understand our communication skills, personality, and overall fit for the company.

My Key Takeaways

One thing I learned from this process is that communication matters just as much as technical knowledge.

Especially during the hackathon, it wasn’t only about building a working project. It was equally important to understand what we were developing, explain our approach confidently, and demonstrate teamwork.

Using AI tools was fine, but being able to explain the AI-generated code and the logic behind it was extremely important.

My advice: Focus on your DSA and SQL basics, revise core CS subjects like OOPs and OS, be thorough with your projects, and most importantly, work on explaining your thought process clearly.

All the best to everyone preparing for placements!
